description: Race registry - see CLAUDE.md's Race Items section for authoring guidelines.

races.name: Dragonborn
races.description:
Dragonborn are proud and noble draconic humanoids, born with the blood of ancient dragons flowing through their veins. They combine the strength and majesty of dragons with humanoid versatility.

Traits: Draconic Ancestry: You have draconic ancestry which determines your breath weapon and damage resistance. Breath Weapon: You can exhale destructive energy once per short rest. Damage Resistance: You have resistance to the damage type associated with your draconic ancestry.

races.name: Gnome
races.description:
Gnomes are small, energetic people driven by boundless curiosity and inventive genius. They delight in discovery and creation, combining keen intellect with playful mischief.

Traits: Gnome Cunning: You have advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against magic. Artificer's Lore: Whenever you make an Intelligence check related to magic items, alchemical objects, or technological devices, you can add double your proficiency. Tinker: You have proficiency with artisan's tools (tinker's tools).

races.name: Half-Orc
races.description:
Half-orcs combine the best qualities of humans and orcs, though some would say they inherit the worst. They possess remarkable physical strength and endurance, along with a fierce will to survive.

Traits: Relentless Endurance: When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 hit point instead (once per long rest). Savage Attacks: When you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack, you can roll one of the weapon's damage dice one additional time. Menacing: You have proficiency in the Intimidation skill.

races.name: Halfling
races.description:
Halflings are a cheerful and practical folk, known for their resourcefulness and uncanny luck. Though small in stature, they possess remarkable courage and a knack for getting out of trouble.

Traits: Lucky: When you roll a 1 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll. Brave: You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened. Halfling Nimbleness: You can move through the space of any creature that is larger than you.

races.name: High Elf
races.description: Ancient and noble elves with strong ties to arcane magic. Scholars, artisans, and mages who value knowledge, magical prowess, and cultural refinement.

races.name: Hill Dwarf
races.description: Stout and sturdy folk who dwell in hills and mountains. Known for their craftsmanship, resilience, and fierce loyalty to clan and kin.

races.name: Mountain Folk
races.description: Hardy people who make their homes in the highest peaks. Miners, climbers, and hunters known for their incredible endurance and connection to the stone.

races.name: Shadowkin
races.description: Mysterious folk touched by shadow, whether through curse, bloodline, or exposure to the Shadow Realm. Often misunderstood, they make excellent spies, scouts, and emissaries.

races.name: Tiefling
races.description:
Tieflings bear the mark of infernal heritage in their appearance and magical abilities. Despite often facing prejudice, many tieflings embrace their dark charisma and innate magical talents.

Traits: Hellish Resistance: You have resistance to fire damage. Infernal Legacy: You know the Thaumaturgy cantrip. You can cast Hellish Rebuke once per long rest, and Darkness once per long rest. Devil's Tongue: Tieflings have a natural gift for persuasion and deception.

races.name: Wood Elf
races.description: Graceful forest dwellers who live in harmony with nature. Expert hunters, scouts, and guardians of the wild places of the world.

races.name: Vashkari
races.description: Vashkari are humanoid folk grown or transformed in the alchemical vats and failed experiments that seep through the dungeon's deeper tunnels. Their flesh is semisolid and faintly translucent, closer in substance to living jelly than to muscle and bone, and it remembers every wound it has ever knit shut. Slow of step but nearly impossible to truly kill, Vashkari are patient tinkerers and unshakeable survivors, equally at home brewing reagents or absorbing a blow that would fell sturdier folk.

races.name: Graveborn
races.description: Graveborn are the dead who did not stay down - risen by an errant necromantic working, a god's mercy, or a stubbornness that outlasted the grave itself - and who kept enough of themselves to walk back into the world as people rather than monsters. Cold to the touch and slow to tire, they carry the memory of the tomb in their bones: little frightens a Graveborn who has already died once, and little exhausts a body that no longer strictly needs to breathe.

races.name: Cindral
races.description: Cindral trace their ancestry to a bloodline touched by raw elemental force - a family line blessed, cursed, or bound by an elemental spirit generations ago. Sparks skitter along their skin when they're angry, and their breath fogs with heat or frost depending on their mood. They burn hot, move fast, and rarely stay calm for long, but that same volatility makes them formidable in a fight and hard to pin down.

races.name: Choir-born
races.description: Choir-born are raised from childhood inside the hidden sects that whisper to the Hollow Star and the things that answer it - taught to chant in unison, to read omens in candle-smoke, and to give themselves over fully to whatever their order demands. Most who leave the choir carry the training with them for life: an unshakeable conviction, a voice that can fill a room, and an ear tuned to things most people are better off not hearing.

races.name: Wildkin
races.description: Wildkin are born in or driven early into the dungeon's feral warrens - raised alongside wolves, bonded to a cave spider's brood, or simply gone half-wild from years spent surviving among the beasts that hunt these tunnels. They move like their animal kin: low to the ground, fast to react, and always aware of what's circling just out of torchlight. Civilized folk find them a little unsettling company. The beasts don't.

races.name: Starspawn
races.description: Starspawn carry something not of this world folded into their bloodline - a touch of the abyss that answered a summoning, brushed a birth, or simply seeped up through the stone one generation too close to a rift. Their thoughts run at odd angles to everyone else's, drifting toward geometries and certainties that don't quite belong here, but that same alien clarity lets them shrug off the fear and confusion that unravels ordinary minds.

races.name: Warrenkin
races.description: Warrenkin come from the sprawling goblin-run tunnels that riddle the dungeon's upper levels - warrens of rope bridges, salvaged scrap, and a hundred half-finished traps. Small, quick, and endlessly resourceful, they're raised to solve problems with cunning long before they're strong enough to solve them with force. A Warrenkin who's lived to adulthood has usually out-thought something much bigger than themselves at least once, and remembers exactly how they did it.
